sections.title: Understanding the Problem
points: The service matches riders with nearby available drivers. It then tracks acceptance, pickup, and trip completion.
Driver locations change frequently and can tolerate some delay. Driver assignment requires stronger consistency.

sections.title: Functional Requirements
points: A rider can request a fare estimate from a pickup point and destination.
The rider can accept the estimate and request a nearby driver.
A driver can accept or reject the offer. After acceptance, the driver receives pickup and destination details.

sections.title: Non-functional Requirements
points: Matching should complete or fail within one minute. Location data must be fresh enough to select useful candidates.
A driver must not receive incompatible assignments. A ride must not commit to multiple drivers.
The scenario includes surges of 100,000 requests from one location. Retain requests and recover from worker or connection failures.

sections.title: Core Entities
points: Rider and Driver contain their identities, relevant profile information, and availability state.
Fare stores the route inputs, quoted price, and estimated time. The server retrieves it by its identifier.
DriverLocation stores recent coordinates and the last accepted update time.
Ride stores the rider, fare, route, assigned driver, and lifecycle state. An offer records its driver, token, and deadline.

sections.title: API
points: POST /fare requests an estimate for a pickup point and destination. The response includes the stored fare ID.
POST /rides accepts a fare ID. A stable request ID can prevent duplicate rides after a timeout.
POST /drivers/location updates coordinates. The server obtains the driver ID from the authenticated session.
PATCH /rides/{rideId} accepts or rejects an offer. An offer token prevents a late response from applying to a newer offer.
Clients can request current ride state after reconnecting. Notifications alone do not prove the current assignment.

sections.title: 1) Estimate and request
points: The Ride Service requests route distance and travel time from the Mapping Service. It applies pricing and stores the Fare.
A confirmed fare ID creates a requested Ride in the database. The Ride Service then starts matching.
An estimate does not reserve a driver. The reliable-matching deep dive adds a queue to protect the later workflow.

diagrams.caption: Riders should be able to request a ride based on the estimated fare

flows.title: Estimate a fare
steps: The Rider Client sends pickup and destination coordinates through the API Gateway.
The Ride Service requests distance and travel time from the Mapping Service.
The Ride Service calculates the fare. It stores the Fare record in the database.
The service returns the estimate and fare ID. No driver is reserved at this point.

flows.title: Create a ride from the stored fare
steps: The rider confirms the fare and sends its ID through the API Gateway.
The Ride Service validates the request and retrieves the stored fare.
It creates a Ride with requested status. It then starts the matching flow.
The client receives the ride ID and waits for status updates. The later queue protects matching work after this stage.

sections.title: 2) Match and accept
points: The Location Service supplies nearby available drivers. The Ride Matching Service ranks candidates by proximity and other selection rules.
The Notification Service sends the offer to a driver through APNs or FCM. A rejection moves to the next candidate.
The Ride Service records acceptance and returns pickup details. The consistency deep dive protects this transition against competing requests.
A delayed acceptance must match the current offer and deadline. It must not replace a newer assignment.

diagrams.caption: Upon request, riders should be matched with a driver who is nearby and available

flows.title: Offer a ride in the initial design
steps: The Ride Matching Service asks the Location Service for nearby available drivers.
It ranks the candidates and selects the next driver.
The Notification Service sends the offer through APNs or FCM.
The Driver Client accepts or rejects the offer through the API Gateway.
The Ride Service records acceptance and returns pickup details. A rejection moves the matching flow to another candidate.
This initial flow needs the reservation checks in the consistency deep dive to prevent competing assignments.

sections.title: 1) Location ingestion and proximity
points: Redis stores current driver locations and supports geographic queries. Keep this high-volume state separate from durable trip records.
Geographic partitioning limits each search. Include neighboring cells or shards when a rider is near a boundary.
Record the last update time and exclude old samples. A cleanup process removes stale locations from the geographic index.
Redis location state can recover from new driver updates. Ride and assignment records still need durable storage.

flows.title: Refresh a driver's searchable location
steps: The Driver Client sends coordinates through its authenticated session.
The Location Service validates the sample and rejects an update older than the accepted position.
It updates the driver's position and last-update information in Redis.
A nearby-driver query searches the relevant geographic area. It excludes stale locations and unavailable drivers.
The matching workflow still claims a driver separately. A search result is not an assignment.

sections.title: 2) Manage update volume
points: The Driver Client adjusts its update interval using movement and activity. A stationary driver can report less often.
Coalesce repeated positions where only the newest sample matters. Reject updates that are older than the accepted position.
Keep a location freshness target. Reduced update volume must not leave matching dependent on obsolete coordinates.

sections.title: 3) Prevent double assignment
points: Atomically claim a driver before sending an offer. The source uses a Redis lock with a short acceptance timeout.
A lock expiry alone does not stop an old worker. Final assignment must also check current ownership and driver availability.
Commit the ride and driver states within the chosen consistency boundary. Only the current offer can release its reservation.
A rejection or timeout permits another candidate. An old acceptance must fail its token or version check.

flows.title: Reserve and confirm a driver
steps: The Ride Matching Service attempts a short reservation for the selected driver in Redis.
If the claim succeeds, it sends an offer with a unique token and deadline.
The driver accepts that specific offer. The service rechecks the deadline, token, and current driver state.
The service commits the assignment conditionally. A stale worker or expired offer cannot replace a newer assignment.
A rejection or timeout releases only the current reservation. The workflow can then try another candidate.

sections.title: 4) Reliable matching and timeouts
points: The Match Queue retains requested rides until processing completes. Queue-based recovery protects against sudden demand and worker failure.
Partition work geographically and scale matching workers independently. Prevent a slow request from blocking all later requests.
Keep offer deadlines in durable state. A delayed task checks the current offer before retrying or releasing a driver.
Temporal or Step Functions can manage retries and timeouts as an alternative workflow implementation. They are not shown in the source diagram.
Retry within a bounded matching policy. Expand the candidate search where useful, then report failure when the policy ends.
Client notifications describe a change. A reconnecting client still fetches authoritative ride state.

flows.title: Recover queued matching work
steps: The Ride Service persists the requested ride and places recoverable matching work in the Match Queue.
A matching worker receives the ride ID and checks its current state.
The worker continues candidate selection and offer handling. It records the result before acknowledging completed work.
A failed worker leaves unfinished work available for retry. The next attempt resumes from durable ride and offer state.
A delayed timeout handler checks the current offer before releasing a reservation or selecting another driver.

sections.title: Final Design
points: The Ride Service stores fares and rides. Redis location data supplies candidates to the Ride Matching Service.
The Match Queue protects pending work. Short driver reservations and conditional assignment prevent conflicting matches.
The Notification Service sends driver offers. Durable ride state and timeout handling connect matching, acceptance, pickup, and completion.
